title: The Graveyard Giant of Lanka: Never Look Back
description:
Sena, a night shift worker, thought he knew the dark roads of his village. But one night, passing the ancient cemetery, he felt a presence. The old tales of Mahasona, the graveyard giant, came rushing back, along with one terrifying warning: never, ever look back.

This episode of Ceylon Dread delves into the rich Sinhala folklore of Sri Lanka, retelling a chilling encounter with the legendary Mahasona. Join us as we explore the shadows that cling to our old burial grounds.
fiction_note: Based on Sri Lankan folklore; characters and events are dramatised.

scenes.narration: Have you ever felt it? That sudden cold spot, even on a sweltering tropical night, when you walk past an old, forgotten cemetery? A chill that has nothing to do with the wind, but everything to do with what lies beneath the earth. Tonight, we speak of such a chill, and the ancient warning that comes with it. Sena knew this feeling well. Every other night, his shift ended at two in the morning. Every time, his path home took him past the old burial ground, tucked away behind the tea plantations, just outside the main village road. Usually, it was just... a cemetery. A place of quiet rest. But not tonight. The air felt heavy.
visuals: Empty, misty village road at 2:30 AM, glowing yellow light from a distant kerosene lamp, silhouettes of coconut trees and a distant old cemetery wall, 50mm film grain, tripod shot
Close up on wet red earth road, faint glint of distant moonlight on puddles, sound of crickets, heavy ground mist, 85mm film, low angle

scenes.narration: He had walked this route for years, his tuk-tuk parked at the factory gate, walking the last mile home. Sena wasn't a superstitious man. He’d seen enough of the world, he thought, to dismiss old village tales. But the old people, they always spoke of this cemetery. They said it was ancient, older than the church or even the biggest temple in the area. They spoke of the giant banyan tree at its heart, its roots like grasping fingers, reaching deep into the soil, touching places no living thing should disturb. And always, always, they whispered of Mahasona, the graveyard giant.
visuals: Distant silhouette of a solitary figure walking on a misty red-earth path, the colossal, ancient banyan tree's canopy looming over an old cemetery wall in the background, moonlight barely piercing the fog, 35mm film, wide shot
Close up on the gnarled, thick roots of an ancient banyan tree, half-buried in cracked earth near an old stone cemetery wall, thick ground mist, faint moonlight, 100mm film, shallow depth of field

scenes.narration: Tonight, the mist wasn't just in the paddy fields. It had crept up the road, hugging the old cemetery wall, swirling around his ankles. The familiar chirping of crickets seemed muted, distant. Even the frogs in the nearby pond were silent. All he could hear was the soft scuff of his worn slippers on the damp earth. Then, the air around him dropped. Not gradually. Suddenly. Like he had stepped into a cold room on a scorching day. And then, he felt it. A breath, cold and clammy, on the back of his neck. He shuddered, pulling his thin sarong tighter.
visuals: A figure (Sena) with back to camera, walking past a low, crumbling cemetery wall, ground mist swirling around his legs, the banyan tree's dark silhouette visible above, distant sound of temple drums, 85mm film, eye-level shot
Close up, from behind, on the nape of a man's neck, hair slightly ruffled, the suggestion of cold air raising goosebumps, blurred misty background of an old cemetery, low light, 135mm film

scenes.narration: Sena quickened his pace, his heart beginning to beat a heavy rhythm against his ribs. It was just the mist, he told himself. Just the night air. But the cold stayed. It was a localised cold. And then, he heard it. A faint rustle. Not leaves blown by the wind. Something... moving. Deliberately. Just behind him. The sound was like heavy cloth dragging on the damp earth, or perhaps, dry bones shifting. He swallowed hard. The hair on his arms stood on end. He was being followed. He could feel its immense presence, right there, behind him.
visuals: Sena's hurried footsteps on a wet, red-earth path, blurred ground mist and the dark outlines of cemetery trees in the background, a feeling of being watched, 50mm film, low angle
A faint, indistinct, tall shadow cast on the ground mist and the cemetery wall, extending from just behind the viewer's perspective, no clear source of light, a feeling of dread, 35mm film

scenes.narration: The old stories came flooding back. His Aachchi, his grandmother, had told them to him countless times, sitting by the sputtering kerosene lamp. “Mahasona,” she would whisper, her voice barely audible, “the giant born of a warrior’s spirit, who haunts the burial grounds. He is immense, child. His head is like a coconut, his eyes glow red, and he smells of the grave.” She’d warned him, fiercely. “If you feel him behind you, if you hear him, never, ever look back. If you do, he will take your life force. You will be Mahasona’s next companion, wandering the cemetery forever.”
visuals: A weathered, aged hand with faint lines (like an old woman's hand) holding a flickering kerosene lamp, casting long shadows on a textured, mud-plastered wall, a sense of an old story being told, 85mm film, shallow depth of field

A silhouette of an old woman's head, partially obscured by shadow, speaking into a young boy's ear (back of head visible), firelight from a hearth creating warm tones in a dark, simple village home, 50mm film

scenes.narration: He was halfway past the cemetery now. The air felt like lead. The sounds behind him grew clearer. A dragging sound. A heavy, uneven shuffle. And then, a low, guttural growl, right at his ear. The sound vibrated through his very bones. It was a sound of ancient hunger, of immense power. He could feel warm, stale breath against his neck now, not cold. A foul odour, like damp earth and something long dead, filled his nostrils. Sena squeezed his eyes shut for a fleeting moment, a silent plea escaping his lips. His legs burned, urging him faster, faster.
visuals: A wide shot of Sena, back to camera, running frantically along a dark, misty cemetery wall, the banyan tree a huge, menacing presence in the background, distant yellow-orange light of a village kopi kade, 35mm film, low angle
Close-up on the back of Sena's neck and ear, slightly glistening with sweat, a blur of dark, heavy mist behind him, the suggestion of a foul breath on his skin, 100mm film

scenes.narration: His entire being screamed at him to turn around. Just a quick glance. Just to know. What could be so terrifying that it couldn't be faced? But Aachchi’s words echoed louder than the growling. *Never look back*. His neck muscles tensed, fighting the overwhelming urge to twist his head. He could feel it now, the immense height of it. A vast, dark shadow that blocked out the dim moonlight, even through the thick canopy of the banyan tree. It was right there. Towering over him. A colossal presence, pressing in, heavy, suffocating.
visuals: Sena's silhouette, head bowed, resisting the urge to turn, against a backdrop of dense, dark foliage and a massive, indistinct shadow stretching beyond the frame, ground mist thick around his feet, 85mm film

A high-contrast shot of a man's clenched fist and arm, veins prominent, knuckles white, indicating intense internal struggle, blurred background of a dark, misty path, 135mm film, shallow depth of field

scenes.narration: He focused on the faint, flickering light ahead. The kerosene lamp of Somapala `appa’s` kopi kade. A beacon of humanity. Just a few more yards. The heavy footsteps behind him mirrored his own, a mocking echo. Shuff... shuff... His own breath came in ragged gasps. The air grew thicker, colder again, like the grave itself was opening up behind him. That ancient, decaying smell intensified, filling his head, making him light-headed. He could almost hear the rasp of its breath, the subtle sound of its immense body shifting, right there, inches behind him.
visuals: Sena's back to camera, running towards a small, glowing yellow light in the distance (kopi kade), the dark, misty cemetery wall and trees on one side, long exposure, 50mm film
Close up on the flickering, smoky flame of a simple kerosene lamp inside a small, rustic shop, casting warm light on rough wooden surfaces, blurred silhouette of a man outside, 100mm film

scenes.narration: And then, suddenly, he was past it. Past the last crumbling stone of the cemetery wall. He stumbled, almost falling, catching himself against a young mango tree, gasping, coughing. He didn't look back. Not even now, when the oppressive presence began to recede, slowly, like a vast, dark wave pulling back from the shore. He could still feel it. That lingering watchfulness. A sense of immense eyes, unseen, following his every ragged breath as he stumbled away, into the relative safety of the village road, leaving the cemetery and its monstrous guardian behind.
visuals: Sena, back to camera, hunched over, hands on his knees, gasping for breath at the edge of the cemetery wall, looking towards the village, the distant banyan tree and mist behind him, 35mm film, wide shot
Close up on Sena's trembling hands clutching the rough bark of a young mango tree, blurred background of receding mist, sound of his heavy breathing, 85mm film

scenes.narration: He collapsed onto a worn wooden bench at Somapala appa’s kopi kade, still trembling, his chest heaving. The old vendor, wiping down his counter with a damp cloth, looked at Sena’s pale, sweat-streaked face. “Rough night, putha?” he asked, pouring a steaming cup of strong, sweet plain tea. Sena could only shake his head, unable to speak, his throat tight with unspoken terror. The warmth of the tea was a comfort, but it couldn't chase away the deep, pervasive cold that had settled in his bones. He felt... marked. Like something had touched him, and would never truly let go.
visuals: Sena, back to camera, slumped on a wooden bench at a rustic kopi kade, facing a counter, the old vendor's back visible as he pours tea, soft yellow light from hanging bulbs, 50mm film
A close-up of a steaming cup of plain tea on a rough wooden counter, Sena's trembling hand reaching for it, blurred background of the kopi kade's interior, 85mm film

scenes.narration: Sena never took that road again after dark. Not a single time. He always took the longer route, adding an extra hour to his journey, even if it meant less sleep. Some things, he knew, were simply not worth the risk. But sometimes, late at night, when the village was utterly silent, a deep chill would settle around him, and he would hear it. That faint, heavy shuffling. That low, guttural growl. And he would feel that immense, cold presence, just behind him. He knew he didn't look back. But he also knew, with a certainty that chilled him to his core, that something of Mahasona, the graveyard giant, had followed him home that night. Just a whisper. A cold, constant reminder. The fear, it stays. Always.
visuals: A winding, dark village road stretching into the distance, a lone tuk-tuk headlight beam cutting through heavy ground mist, no cemetery in sight, a sense of lingering dread, 35mm film, long exposure
Close-up on a dark, slightly open window in a simple village house, a faint shadow playing on the curtains, sound of distant gecko calls, a feeling of being watched from the outside, 100mm film

shorts.title: The Graveyard's Breath: Never Turn Around!
shorts.narration: Imagine walking home late, the village silent except for your own footsteps. You pass the old cemetery, and the air drops, suddenly, unnaturally cold. Then, you feel it: a distinct breath, cold and clammy, on the back of your neck. You speed up, but the sound of heavy shuffling follows. The old stories of Mahasona, the graveyard giant, scream in your mind: never, ever look back. But the urge… the overwhelming urge to turn and see what immense, dark presence is right behind you, it’s almost unbearable. You can feel its towering shadow, its foul breath. What would you do? Could you resist? The full story is on our channel.

Vertical shot: Close-up from behind, on a person's neck and ear, suggesting a cold breath, blurred misty background, 85mm film
Vertical shot: A low angle on hurried footsteps on a wet, red-earth path, ground mist swirling, 35mm film

shorts.title: The Shadow That Followed Me Home
shorts.narration: You've just escaped the most terrifying walk of your life. You ran, never looking back, past the ancient cemetery where they say the giant Mahasona roams. Your heart is pounding, your body trembling, but you made it. You're safe, or so you think. But even as you stumble into the faint lights of the village, that lingering cold, that sense of immense eyes watching you, refuses to fade. You never turned around. You never saw what was there. But you *feel* it. That dark presence, a subtle, chilling reminder that some shadows, once encountered, follow you home. Always. The full story is on our channel.
visuals: Vertical shot: Silhouette of a person, back to camera, slumped against a tree at the edge of a misty cemetery, looking towards distant village lights, 50mm film
Vertical shot: A close-up of a trembling hand holding a warm cup of tea at a rustic village shop, blurred background, 85mm film
Vertical shot: A dark, winding village road, a single tuk-tuk headlight beam cutting through thick ground mist, a sense of eerie quiet, 35mm film
Vertical shot: Close-up on a dark, slightly ajar window of a village house, a subtle, unidentifiable shadow falling across the curtain, 100mm film
Vertical shot: A lone, flickering kerosene lamp in a dark, empty street, casting long, dancing shadows, 50mm film
